diet.text: Small frogs, toads, small fish and earthworms

overview.text: The Checkered Garter Snake is a garter snake of the south-western United States, Mexico and Central America with a bold black checkerboard pattern. It has a very mild venom that is harmless to people.

identification.text: Usually greenish with a distinct black checkerboard pattern down the back.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually 46 to 61 cm (18 to 24 in), but up to 107 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The south-western USA (Kansas and Oklahoma to Texas, New Mexico, Arizona and California), Mexico, and Central America south to Costa Rica.

habitat.text: Desert, grassland, shrubland and forest, usually close to water, up to about 2,200 m.

behaviour.text: Unlike most garter snakes it is partly active at night. If grabbed it smears a smelly liquid on its attacker rather than biting.

diet.text: Small frogs, toads, small fish and earthworms.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to live young; there is evidence that females can sometimes reproduce without males.

recognise.text: Black checkerboard pattern on a greenish body.
